title: Also Small Models Can Reasonably Self-Evaluate Their Confidence
abstract: arXiv:2609.39478v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This study systematically evaluates self-evaluation-based uncertainty quantification across different language models of varying sizes on question-answering tasks spanning general to specialized knowledge domains. Using various self-evaluation methods where models judge their own predictions, we examine how model scale and domain specificity affect the quality of self-assessed confidence signals. Our results reveal that while accuracy predictably declines with smaller models and more specialized domains, the reliability of self-evaluated confidence remains largely stable across both dimensions. This independence means the most capable model is not necessarily the best at self-assessing prediction reliability. These findings suggest that smaller models can achieve reasonable self-assessed confidence despite lower accuracy, making them viable for resource-constrained deployments.

translated_title: 小模型也能合理地自我评估其置信度
translated_abstract: 这项研究系统性地评估了基于自我评估的不确定性量化在不同规模语言模型上的表现，涵盖从通用知识到专业知识领域的问答任务。通过使用多种自我评估方法（即模型对自己的预测进行评判），我们研究了模型规模和领域专业化程度如何影响自评估置信度信号的质量。结果显示，虽然准确率随着模型变小和领域更加专业化而可预见地下降，但自评估置信度的可靠性在这两个维度上基本保持稳定。这种独立性意味着最强大的模型并不一定在自我评估预测可靠性方面表现最好。这些发现表明，尽管准确率较低，较小的模型仍能实现合理的自评估置信度，使其成为资源受限部署场景的可行选择。
tldr: 研究发现小语言模型虽然准确率较低，但其自我评估置信度的可靠性与大模型基本相当，因此小模型同样适合在资源受限的场景中部署使用。
en_tdlr: Smaller language models can self-evaluate their confidence as reliably as larger models despite lower accuracy, making them viable for resource-constrained deployments.
